chapter: Second interview: bass, Parker and Miles
title: Seeing Charlie Parker put people down
summary: Mingus lost enthusiasm for playing because there was nowhere to blow; Parker barred a player from the stand and mocked Mel Torme.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: But you were saying that you enjoyed playing bass when you were coming up. What sort of -- when did the enthusiasm begin to lessen to some extent?
It lessened (inaudible) I wasn't interested in going with the guys.

Because there was nowhere to blow. And (inaudible) with Charlie Parker in ______. That was a long time ago. I remember, the first time I saw him -- the second time I saw him put somebody down. G. G. ______ was
there, and he wouldn't allow G.G. on the bandstand with him.
I don't know, I didn't ask him.
And another time he put somebody down was Mel Torme, was Berlin on drums. And he kept saying, Mickey Rooney, Mickey Rooney.
